## 0 Standing rules, the machine, and the Mac corrections

### 0.1 The owner's standing rules for the build (J156, J157)

1. **Design = reference.** A choice where the design is unclear is one row of `choices.md` (id, date, seat, section,
   choice, reason, the test that holds it); rows are append-only; a reversal is a new row naming the row it supersedes.
2. **Staging.** M0 builds each piece's basic case and names what it defers and to which milestone (§4b).
3. **No new design.** A scope line stands until M1.
4. **The machine.** The reference machine of §12.1 itself (facts in 0.2). pnpm is never global: every command is
   `corepack pnpm …` (C-0030).
5. **Timings.** A timing taken in §12.1's timing phase on this machine — otherwise idle, on AC power, after 30 s idle,
   batches ≤ 60 s, `bench/calibrate` before and after within 5 % — is **AUTHORITATIVE**; one taken while other seats run
   is **CONTENDED** and never gates (C-0025, C-0047). Timing bars run in a wave of their own with nothing else running,
   whose first act records the reference score (C-0075); a miss is answered by its pre-decided fallback in the owning
   item's fix round (T-fix) and re-measured in the conditional re-run wave T2, alone, before the record (C-0080). The
   contention detector counts **every** process on the machine — M-1's Chrome sessions and Python measurements among
   them (J159) — and the session opens the timing phase (`TIMING-PHASE OPEN <token>` in the lane log, `PLAT_TIMING_TOKEN`
   to the script) only after M-1's research-side seats are paused (C-0103). The tiers are timed by C-0097's protocol:
   the PR tier gates on its batched sum (≤ 60 s batches), the projected tiers run once whole with one bounded repeat.
6. **Disk.** The data volume held 2.6 GB free when the build started and 18 GB after the owner's cache clearing
   (2026-10-03): one pnpm store (the default), no git worktrees, bench and log output to
   `/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-cstokes-Desktop-Maps/2367ceda-b0ec-4fa5-94a3-059f82e2d4b7/scratchpad/build/`
   (`PLAT_BENCH_OUT`), truncated; no browser download beyond the cached builds (C-0028, C-0051); a seat that sees
   under 1 GB free (`df -h /Users/cstokes`) stops and reports. Outputs go out; **inputs never come from the scratchpad**
   (C-0067).
7. **M-1 runs beside M0** in its research-side lane. A piece that needs the reference recordings or M-1's baselines is
   **AFTER-M-1**: never parked, faked or estimated. Two start conditions (C-0071): **(a)** when
   `plat/packages/testkit/baselines/baselines.json` and the digest `plat/docs/digest/` are committed with their
   `CrossingRecord`s (and `denylist.json` for the content scanner), **(b)** when `ng-faces.json` (C-0043 — this spec's
   request to M-1, not in §16's M-1 row) is committed, or M-1 records that it cannot deliver it, in which case the
   clauses that need it become descriptive by §13.5's ⟨M-1⟩ rule. §1 names every row and digest entry needed.
   **A crossing** — M-1's `baselines.json`, `ng-faces.json`, `denylist.json` or a digest file entering `plat/` — lands
   only while a build or AFTER-M-1 wave is open (never in T, T-fix or T2, never between a wave's close and the next
   snapshot), a numbers-only file only after M0-k-05 has LANDED (`corepack pnpm baselines:check`); its countersigning
   seat appends its `CrossingRecord` to `crossings.json` and signs its ledger row, and the wave's close attributes the
   file by that record (C-0120). A job that reads an M-1 file stays pending until the file's reviewing items have run on
   it (C-0121).
8. **Clean room (§17.1 (1)).** Implementer-side seats read only `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/volumes/INDEX.md`, the
   volumes a milestone builds (M0: none), `plat/` and `plat/docs/digest/`, published papers and the public documentation
   of adopted libraries. On this machine the whole reference corpus is present, so the firewall is physical: every
   search, find, grep, du or ls runs inside `plat/` or on a named design file — never recursively from the project root
   or `docs/` — and never follows a symbolic link out of `plat/`. Every seat signs `plat/CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2 before its
   work lands (its row: seat, date, role, what it read).
9. **Working rules for every seat.** Save as you go; a CHECKPOINT line in `docs/lane-events.log` at least every twenty
   minutes; when complete, `corepack pnpm landed -- <item id> --lane <lane key>` (the landed record `plat/docs/build/landed/<item id>.json`:
   every created and changed file with its SHA-256 against the wave's snapshot, C-0104), then a LANDED line naming the
   record and its files; long command output to the scratchpad build directory; commit and push nothing (the session
   commits after each wave). The only writes outside an item's `owns` are the permitted appends — a `choices.md` row, a
   `CLEAN-ROOM.md` row of §2, §3, §4 or §5, a `CrossingRecord` appended to `crossings.json` (C-0120), the one index line
   of C-0064 and the landed record — under the id rule (re-read the
   last id immediately before appending, append in one write; a collision is renumbered by the next writer, C-0104). A
   LANDED item whose checker returns FIX re-runs under `<lane>-fix<n>` on the checker's list, editing only its own files.

### 0.2 The machine (probed 2026-10-03; receipts in the lane log)

MacBookAir10,1 (fanless), Apple M1 — 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores — 16 GB, macOS 14.7.8 (23H730); Node 24.12.0
arm64 (V8 13.6.233.17) as a universal binary whose x86_64 slice runs under Rosetta 2 as a genuine x64 V8
(`arch -x86_64 node` → `process.arch` `x64`, same version and V8); npm 11.6; corepack 0.34.5; Apple clang 16.0.0
(arm64; `-arch x86_64` cross-compiles, `arch -x86_64` runs it); no `pnpm` on PATH; Playwright cache at
`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`: chromium 1223 and 1243 (with their headless shells), firefox 1522, webkit
`mac14_arm64_special` 2251 — `playwright-core` 1.60.0 is the one release whose three browsers are all cached (C-0051);
outbound HTTP 200 from `registry.npmjs.org`, `nodejs.org`, `www.netlib.org/fdlibm/` and `prng.di.unimi.it` (the
Playwright CDN answers but is not used); on AC power; 18 GB free of 228 GB (2.6 GB before the owner's cache clearing).

## 1 Scope — M0's pieces (a)–(f): now, AFTER-M-1, and the timing bars

Legend: **NOW** = built and judged on this machine in M0's waves; **TIMING** = a bar measured in the timing-phase wave
(M0-t-01) by §12.1's protocol; **AFTER-M-1 (a)** = needs `baselines.json` and the digest (and `denylist.json` for the
scanner); **AFTER-M-1 (b)** = needs `ng-faces.json` (C-0071). "Here" in §2's bar lists means NOW.

### (a) `@plat/kernel` (§3, §2.2) — NOW
Lattice, snapping, exact predicates, one arena per layer with the five levels as views, role and owner tables and
reference resolution, attraction and contact semantics, batched transactions with stage-end index partitions, booleans /
buffers / bands on the arrangement with the CI oracles, OBB / hull / LIR / regular fit, snap rounding, the straight
skeleton with its validator and exact OBB roofs, the sampled medial axis, warp and smoothing, the invariant suite, the
arena block (C-0037), the noise module (C-0065), the kernel's shared types (C-0112) and the façade. Items M0-a-01 … M0-a-16.
* Bars NOW: B-FUZZ 0 crashes / hangs / invalid outputs on 10⁶ random inputs per primitive and on M0's constructive set
  (C-0038; §13.1); §3.7 (i)'s differential oracle agreement (unattracted: equal face counts and symmetric difference
  ≤ perimeter × 1 cm; attracted: valid and ≤ perimeter × √2 · `attractCm`; ≥ 10⁵ unattracted cases per operation);
  §3.8's fixture bar (0 crashes, 0 validator failures); the corpus bar (downgrades ≤ 0.5 %, work-limit hits ≤ 0.1 %) on
  the stand-in corpus (C-0015) — the synthetic footprints at M0-a-12, the spikes' district and water faces re-run by
  M0-c-06 and M0-e-06 in-process (C-0067), B-CITY-lite at M1; op-order determinism (the declared form at M0-a-06, the
  callback issue order and slot-renumbering identity at M0-d-08; §13.2); save → load → save byte-identical on the arena
  block; §13.1's ladder coverage — the kernel ladders (F-SKELETON's downgrades, F-NUM's kernel side) at M0-k-04, and
  every rung of the stage ladders M0 builds (F-CUT, F-ROUTE, F-NUM's re-propose, F-RIVER, F-WALL, F-BUDGET-STAGE, F-WORK's
  declared coarser rungs) at **M0-x-05**, forced by fixtures on the real stages after they land (C-0085).
* Bars TIMING: insert + snap + attract + re-walk ≤ 8 µs per growth proposal; `splitFace` per bent cut against §12.4's
  S8 row (≈ 12 µs); §3.7 (ii): S9's corridor bands over the CITY face set against §12.4's S9 row (25 ms) and one
  district ≤ 3 ms; S11's geometry share ≤ 3 µs per plot median on a synthetic per-plot workload (the kernel calls §3.7
  names, built and tested by M0-k-04, C-0107; re-measured at M1 on B-CITY-lite's S11); skeleton ≤ 20 µs median per
  footprint. A miss takes **C-0098's ordered ladder**, each step a T-fix round and a T2 re-measure (C-0026, C-0080):
  one optimisation pass → ≤ 2× the measured cost carried into its §12.4 row (a declared budget amendment inside the
  row's budget) / > 2× or over the row's budget the WebAssembly accelerator for that loop → still missing: for the
  arrangement bars (`corridorUnion`; S11's `offsetFace` part) Clipper2-WASM as the only engine on every host (§3.7 (ii),
  a declared golden shift), for every other loop the D-18 budget re-declaration for the owner's veto; at most three
  cycles per bar, each recorded in the M0 record.
* AFTER-M-1: none.

### (b) The bent-cut transaction with the hole slit (§4.6; items 34–41) — NOW, the NG comparison AFTER-M-1
The planner (steps 1–7), the transaction with its ladder (step 8), width (9), continuation (10), recursion (11), the
deep-interior rule and the seam portals, the S8 stage, and the NG comparison harness built NOW on synthetic files (M0-b-05,
C-0117). Items M0-b-01 … M0-b-05; AFTER-M-1 the run items M0-b-05a (a) and M0-b-05b (b).
* Bars NOW: T34-1's commit clause (every block S8 commits has an OBB minor extent below the `τ` drawn for its face and
  every face it cut one at or above it, replayed from the `cut.stop` draws — M0-b-03), T36-1, T37-1, T38-1's shape
  clauses, T39-1, T40-1, T41-1 on the M0 (b) synthetic face set (curved, round-joined, triangular, C-shaped and holed
  faces) in the PR tier, T34-1's 10 000-face mean (`g` within 7/30 ± 3 s.e.) nightly (M0-b-04; the τ formula's range
  `τ ∈ [e_lo, e_hi]` is M0-b-02's unit test, not T34-1); F-CUT's bars: on 10⁵ random concave and holed faces the ladder ends in ≤ 6 kernel calls, the face count
  never decreases, each district's substitution residue ≤ 5 % (soft); 0 lanes cross a wall strip; **§16 M0 (b)'s corner
  clause (within 0.10 of mid-course on ≥ 80 %) and arrival clause (≥ 85° on ≥ 95 %)** on the M0 (b) faces (C-0073 —
  absolute thresholds on ours, judged now by M0-b-04).
* Bars TIMING: `splitFace` per cut (above).
* **AFTER-M-1 (a)** (M0-b-05a; needs exactly): (1) `baselines.json` rows of §13.5's **bent-cut signature** — σ plain
  0.066 and ring 0.098 (± 0.02), the corner share, the arrival share, the fillet share — each with `referenceBuild`
  NG 1.2.2, `metricVersion`, `capture`, `script`, `date`; (2) the digest entry on **how NG's σ was measured** (the
  recorded frame, the rotated retries included); (3) the re-fitted plot-depth rows and regime block-depth minimums
  (item 34, J-A34.01) as cells for `granularity.json` and `regimes.json`, provenance "M-1 ⟨date⟩". From these M0-b-05a
  judges σ ± 0.02 on our faces in the recorded frame and applies the depth rows (verdicts pass / fail / reported — an ⟨M-1⟩
  cell with no row fails, a descriptive row is reported, C-0116).
* **AFTER-M-1 (b)** (M0-b-05b; needs exactly): (4) **`ng-faces.json`** (C-0043, C-0086): NG's recorded face shapes as
  integer-centimetre rings by template with `referenceBuild`, each face record carrying its recorded block areas (cm²),
  cut lengths (cm) and, per recorded cut, the corner's position along its course, the arrival angle and its fillet flag,
  passed through `corepack pnpm baselines:check` (the design's `plat baselines check`, C-0113); (5) §13.5's **blocks** row (NG block counts per template at `medium`, with
  `spreadKS.p90`), the **cut lengths per face** row this spec requests of M-1 (C-0086) and the **bent-cut signature** row

  shapes), the block-area KS against the blocks row and the cut-length KS against the cut-lengths row by the band rule's
  distribution clause in its M0 form (C-0092), re-runs the corner and arrival clauses on NG's shapes against the same
  thresholds (C-0081), and calibrates `cut.flattenM` (J-A37.01). The comparison is **the check of the adopted
  corner-first rule** (§16). Without the file or a field (M-1's recorded statement), the clause that needs it is
  descriptive by §13.5's ⟨M-1⟩ rule (C-0071).

### (c) The fused-layout spike — S4 routing + S5 growth + S8 infill on a flat synthetic site at CITY face counts (§4.3, §4.4, §4.6) — NOW, statistics AFTER-M-1
The flat fixture with its S3 slice (C-0016, C-0032), the trace strategy with the strip stand-in (C-0033), S4 with its
basic water crossing (C-0076), S5a–S5d, S8 through (b), the pipeline (C-0077) and the gate harness. Items M0-c-01 …
M0-c-06, M0-x-02, M0-x-04 and the fusion statistics harness built NOW on synthetic files (M0-c-07, C-0117); AFTER-M-1 the
run items M0-c-07a (a) and M0-c-07b (b).
* Bars NOW: no turn cliff (10 m resampling: no empty bin above 15° while the bin below holds > 1 %); the junction row —
  p5 ≥ 30°, median 85–95°, organic 4-way share 0–15 % — on the flat fixture's L1 junctions (C-0094; re-judged against
  M-1's recomputed band by M0-c-07a); 0 whole-map restarts on 1 000 seeds (the pipeline has no restart path; the harness asserts the report carries none
  and counts every ladder use); the growth-drift row (net turn over 600 m p50 15–30°, > 90° on ≤ 1 %); the face-count
  report (≈ 1 500 cuts, ≈ 25 districts at CITY, §12.4); roads leaving the walled stage = N; S8 ≡ S9 Hausdorff 0; 0
  lanes cross a strip; the skeleton corpus bar re-run on the exported district faces.
* Bars TIMING: S4 + S5 + S8 ≤ 100 ms at CITY, measured in Node and inside Chromium's worker on the same seeds, the
  Chromium figure checked where the two differ by more than ± 15 % (§12.1; C-0082). A miss: extramural growth stops at
  `secondary` (lanes infill-only everywhere, a switch built at M0, set in a T-fix round) and the gate re-runs in T2
  (§4.4; C-0080). R12-4: the CITY per-stage p50 of the S3 slice (≈ 11 ms of §12.4's 16 ms row), S4 (10 ms), S5 (40 ms)
  and S8 (20 ms) REPORTED from the harness's stamps; an exceeding row restated by M0-x-01 in a choices row (C-0084).
* **AFTER-M-1 (a)** (M0-c-07a; needs exactly): §13.5's **junction** row (NG 361 / 361 T; the 4-way share) and the

### (d) The determinism spike (§6) — NOW
Structured stream keys, lineage-hash minting, the Merkle digest with the kernel's level digests, `dmath`, the
time-dilation shim, the allowlist lint with its vendored scan (**wave 1, alone, before any model-package code**,
C-0063), the matching routine, the cross-host harness. Items M0-d-01 … M0-d-09, M0-m-01.
* Bars NOW: digests identical on Node arm64, Node x64 (Rosetta), Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, workers on and off, 100
  seeds of the spike city (C-0028, C-0051); every stream key and lineage hash distinct in the spike city (the
  sky-island clause at M6-sky); time dilation byte-identical; op-order determinism; the known-answer tests of
  xoshiro128\*\*, MurmurHash3 (SMHasher 0xB3ECE62A; `H32` check vectors of §13.6 (2)) and `dmath` on both
  architectures; a full root recomputation equals the maintained root after every batch (the CI oracle); the lint's
  probe red (a model-package file holding `Math.pow`, `Math.random`, `Math.sin`, `Date.now`, `**`,
  `Object.keys().sort()` makes `corepack pnpm lint` exit non-zero naming each line).
* Bars TIMING: ≤ 0.1 µs per structured key; digest maintenance ≤ 5 % of each batch's own time at CITY; root
  finalisation ≤ 5 ms at a stage end; full recomputation ≤ 150 ms at CITY, the records tree (synthetic, C-0015)
  included; matching ≤ 2 µs per point-anchored and ≤ 20 µs per overlap-anchored entity, median, per kind, on M0-d-05b's
  synthetic sets and on M0-d-09's 20 re-derivation pairs of the spike city (old / fresh per kind — the real-anchor
  workload §6.3 names, C-0090). Each has §6.2's / §6.3's pre-decided fallback, none of which moves a golden.
* AFTER-M-1: none. (§12.1's in-Chrome measurement: the fusion and site gates are timed inside Chromium's worker in the
  timing phase through M0-d-06's runner, C-0082, superseding C-0074; §12.3's model budgets are first gated at M1, whose
  nightly re-measures them in Chrome.)

## 2 The work breakdown

Seventy-two items in twenty build waves (0–19), the timing-phase wave (T), its two conditional waves — the fallback fix
rounds (T-fix) and the re-run (T2) — and two AFTER-M-1 waves; at most four implementer seats run at once; T and T2 run
alone, and no AFTER-M-1 item starts while T, T-fix or T2 is open (every one depends on M0-x-01 but M0-k-07, which starts
in the first open build wave after `denylist.json` crosses, C-0121) or beyond the four-seat cap (C-0102). The waves were
computed from the items' `dependsOn` by
a critical-path packer and re-checked by the validator (every dependency lands in an earlier wave; every file has one
owner by directory-prefix matching, hand-overs declared; every test that reads `@plat/testkit` code lies in a test project
that references the test kit, and every dependency's code is importable from a package the item writes or visible from a
test folder it owns — the rules V1 – V3 of C-0122). Each item is one seat's sitting of a few hours. A **run item**
writes no code: it runs a script or harness another item built and tested, applies declared table cells and records
(M0-t-01, M0-t-02, M0-k-07, M0-b-05a, M0-b-05b, M0-c-07a, M0-c-07b; C-0115, C-0117).

**Ownership rules.** No two items own one file, by *prefix*: an item that owns a folder owns everything under it, so a
second item's file inside that folder is a conflict unless the first item's `handsOver` names it. A package's
`src/index.ts`, `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`, the test projects' `tsconfig.json` and `test/scaffold/`, and the
workspace files are the scaffold's (M0-s-01); each module folder's `index.ts` starts empty and passes to the folder's
owner (C-0013), each bench harness folder's `index.ts` likewise (C-0059); a module folder the scaffold did not plan gets
its one index line from its owner (C-0064). Hand-over chains: `workLimits.json` M0-f-03a → M0-f-03b (C-0021);
`granularity.json`, `regimes.json` M0-s-02 → M0-b-05a; `interior.json` M0-s-02 → M0-c-07a; `cut.json` M0-s-02 →
M0-b-05b → M0-c-07b; `bands.json` M0-s-02 → M0-c-07b; `reference-score.json` M0-f-01 → M0-t-01 (C-0075);
`bench/src/tier-jobs/` M0-f-02a → M0-f-02b; `M0-timings.json` M0-t-01 → M0-t-02 (C-0080); `M0-record.json` M0-x-01 →
M0-x-03; `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` M0-s-01 → M0-d-03, `layout/src/pipeline/index.ts` M0-x-02 → M0-x-04 (C-0095; its
`ng-shapes.ts` / `ng-hoods.ts` stub hand-overs are withdrawn by C-0117 — M0-b-05 and M0-c-07 own their folders whole);
`baselines/denylist-allow.json` M0-k-06 → M0-k-07 (C-0101); `kernel/src/types/index.ts` and
`bench/src/{scan,parity,baselines-check}/index.ts`, created empty by the scaffold's fourth fix round → M0-a-01, M0-k-06,
M0-k-05, M0-k-05 (C-0112, C-0113); `kernel/src/arr/index.ts` M0-a-08 → M0-a-09 (M0-a-08's five re-export lines at wave
8, M0-a-09's four appended at wave 9; C-0122, C-0123). Every item's tests live in its own test
folder (`test/<item's folder>/*.test.ts`) — a test of bench code in `bench/test/<harness>/`, owned by the harness folder's
owner, the only test project that references the bench (C-0114); **a test of package code that reads `@plat/testkit` code**
(M0-k-03's oracles, M0-k-01's generators, M0-k-02's set, M0-d-08's harness, M0-k-05's metrics) or an oracle library **in
`packages/testkit/test/<package>/<item folder>/`**, owned by the package item and named in its tests — the testkit test
project is the one package test project that references every package, so it alone compiles such a test (from
`kernel/test` or `layout/test` the import fails `tsc -b` with TS2307 / TS6059 / TS6307); the `<package>` folders `kernel`,
`model`, `tables`, `site` and `layout` there are reserved for package items; such a test reaches the package only through
`@plat/<package>`'s export, so the item exports what it tests; the six at M0: M0-a-08 `kernel/arr-booleans-buffers/`,
M0-a-09 `kernel/arr-bands/`, M0-a-15 `kernel/io/`, M0-b-03 `layout/infill-fabric/`, M0-c-05 `layout/growth-s5cd/`, M0-e-04
`layout/districts/` (C-0122) —, its fixtures under `<package>/test/fixtures/<item>/`, and every harness's
numbers-only summary at `plat/docs/build/summaries/<item>.json` (C-0067). **Attribution (C-0104).** Every item owns
`plat/docs/build/landed/<item id>.json` implicitly: when a wave opens the session runs `corepack pnpm snapshot --
wave-<n>` (every file under `plat/` outside `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `coverage/` and `*.tsbuildinfo` with its SHA-256,
to `landed/snapshots/wave-<n>.json`); when a seat lands it runs `corepack pnpm landed -- <item id> --lane <lane key>`, which hashes every
file under the item's `owns` prefixes and the permitted appends and writes the record (created / changed / unchanged
against the snapshot); the checker verifies the record against the tree and the `owns` list, and at the wave's close
`corepack pnpm landed:verify -- wave-<n>` names any changed file no record of the wave claims. The permitted appends —
a `choices.md` row, a `CLEAN-ROOM.md` row of §2 – §5, a `CrossingRecord` appended to `crossings.json`, C-0064's one index
line, the landed record — follow the id rule (re-read the last id, append in one write, a collision renumbered by the
next writer); a seat that only appended records them with `landed -- <record id> --lane <lane key>` and no `--owns`. M-1's
crossing files (`baselines.json`, `ng-faces.json`, `denylist.json`, a digest file) are attributed at the wave's close by
the `CrossingRecord` appended in that wave whose sha256 matches, claimed through the ledger row its `checkerSeat` names
(C-0120). The full field set per item is in

## 3 The check protocol — how a checker seat accepts an item

A checker seat is implementer-side (it signs `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2 like every seat) and never the item's author.

1. **Read the brief whole.** The item in `M0-work.json`, its entry above, every design section it names (read in full,
   not skimmed), the `choices.md` rows it cites and any rows the author appended.
2. **Read the code whole, and attribute it without git (C-0104).** Every file the item owns. Seats run no git and up to
   four share one tree, so the checker reads the item's landed record `plat/docs/build/landed/<item id>.json` (written
   by the seat with `corepack pnpm landed -- <item id> --lane <lane key>` from the item's `owns` list: every file under those prefixes and
   the permitted appends, each with its SHA-256 and its status created / changed / unchanged against the wave's snapshot
   `landed/snapshots/wave-<n>.json`, the session's file) and verifies (a) every path in the record lies under the item's
   `owns` (matched by directory prefix) or is a permitted append — a `choices.md` row, a `CLEAN-ROOM.md` row of §2 – §5,
   a `CrossingRecord` appended to `crossings.json`, C-0064's one index line, the record itself — with the appended row
   ids listed, and no record lists a crossing file (C-0120); (b) every hash in the record equals the file
   in the tree now (a later change is another seat's and is attributed at the wave's close); (c) at the wave's close,
   `corepack pnpm landed:verify -- wave-<n>` names every file that differs from the snapshot and appears in no landed
   record of the wave — a crossing file excepted when a `CrossingRecord` appended in the wave and claimed names its
   sha256 (C-0120) — an unattributed change fails the wave's check and goes to the session, which alone runs git. A
   touched file outside `owns` and the appends fails the item unless a choices row re-assigned ownership. Two rows
   carrying one id (a collision) are renumbered by the next writer, never by the checker (the id rule, C-0104).
   The checker runs (a) and (b) as `corepack pnpm landed:verify -- wave-<n> --item <item id>` and quotes its output; the
   seat names the files it knows it edited with `--touched <plat/path>`, which `landed` refuses outside `owns` and the
   appends, naming the owner; a seat without an item — the checker for its `checks/<item id>.md`, a spec lane for
   `M0.md` or `M0-work.json` — records its exact files with `corepack pnpm landed -- <record id> --lane <lane key>
   --owns <plat/path>…`, files no item owns, so the wave's close attributes them too (C-0111).
3. **Run the gates**, all as `corepack pnpm …`: `install --frozen-lockfile`; `lint` (the allowlist, dependency direction,
   path rule, vendored scan) **with its `probe-red` check quoted** — the lint's own whole-tree check lints the probe
   fixture `tools/lint/fixtures/probe/zz-probe.ts` in place under the model-package rule set and passes only when every
   planted line (C-0063's list) is reported, so `corepack pnpm lint` green means the probe is red; the checker quotes
   that output and writes no file into a package folder (C-0106); `build` (`tsc -b`); `test --project <package>` and the
   item's own test files — and `test --project testkit` on the item's `packages/testkit/test/<package>/<folder>/` where
   it owns one (C-0122); the item's bars marked *here*
   in `M0-work.json` (B-FUZZ at the PR size for a kernel item; the harness for a spike item); a timing bar is NOT run by
   the checker (the timing-phase waves T and T2 run it) — the checker verifies the harness exists, emits the stamped record and
   refuses to gate on a `contended` result.
4. **The checklist** (each line pass or fail, quoted with evidence):
   * every interface the item lists is present under the design's name and signature (§3.4's list, §14's interfaces);
   * every test id the item lists is implemented and green; every design clause the item names has a test or a named
     reason it cannot have one yet (an AFTER-M-1 or deferred clause names its milestone or its start condition);
   * **no undeclared shortcut**: a stub is a `notBuilt('<milestone>')` with a choices row or a §4b entry; a `TODO`,
     a skipped test without a milestone tag, a silently narrowed bar or a constant where a table cell is required fails;
   * **no undeclared deviation**: where the code departs from a design section, a `choices.md` row exists naming the
     section, the choice and the test; otherwise fail;
   * every table cell carries `unit`, `provenance` and `calibratable`; no `Math` member outside §6.5 (3)'s allowlist in
     a model package (the lint's report quoted; the `probe-red` check's output quoted); no import, fixture, script or
     bench input path resolves outside `plat/` (C-0067); every evidence file the item cites lies under
     `plat/docs/build/`;
   * a test of bench code lies under `bench/test/<harness>/` inside the item's `owns` (C-0114); a run item's landed
     record holds no code file — tables, summaries and records only (C-0115, C-0117);
   * a test that reads `@plat/testkit` code or an oracle library lies under `packages/testkit/test/<package>/<folder>/`
     inside the item's `owns` and imports the package only through `@plat/<package>` (C-0122); such a test placed in a
     package's own test folder fails `tsc -b` (TS2307 / TS6059 / TS6307) and is a checker failure; the item's module
     index exports what the test reads (M0-a-08's `arr/index.ts` lines at its landing, C-0123);
   * the landed record exists, every path in it under `owns` or a permitted append, every hash equal to the tree
     (C-0104); a tier job the item adds carries a derived status, never a written one (C-0099); a vitest test of the
     item spawns no tier script (C-0105);
   * a tier job, parity report or scan the item adds carries one of the three statuses of C-0069; a *pending-after-M-1*
     entry names its file; nothing *built* reads a missing file;
   * the author's `CLEAN-ROOM.md` row exists and lists what the author read; nothing it lists lies outside rule 1;
   * `bugs` empty in every run; no `contended` timing presented as a result.
5. **Verdict** written to `plat/docs/build/checks/<item id>.md`: pass or fail, each checklist line with its evidence
   (command and quoted output), every conclusion labelled CONFIRMED (executed) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned), and the
   checker's ledger row. A failed item returns to its author with the failing lines under the lane key
   `<lane>-fix<n>`; the fix round re-runs the failed lines and the item's whole test set. An item is LANDED only on a
   pass; the lane log carries both lines.

(`build/m0-scaffold-fix4`, C-0113, C-0120, C-0121; landed 2026-10-03, L-0017, before wave 2 opened); the entry marked `¶`

unchanged).

**Package rules (§14).** Dependency direction `kernel ← model ← tables ← {site} ← layout`; `testkit` may import every
package and is imported by nothing shipped; `bench` imports `testkit` and the packages; no model package has DOM types
or Node globals; every adopted runtime library is imported in exactly one adapter file of the one package that uses it
(`kernel/src/adapters/{robust-predicates,flatbush,delaunator,simplex-noise}.ts` — noise is the kernel's, §14, C-0065);
`exports` carry the `plat-source` condition (C-0013). The lint enforces all of it (M0-d-07).

**Dependencies, pinned exactly (§17.4 as amended by C-0062; registry on 2026-10-03).** Production closure (vendored,
scanned): `robust-predicates` 3.0.3 (Unlicense), `flatbush` 4.6.2 (ISC), `flatqueue` 3.1.0 (ISC, through flatbush),
`delaunator` 5.1.0 (ISC), `simplex-noise` 4.0.3 (MIT). Dev: `typescript` 6.0.3 (C-0014), `typescript-eslint` 8.71.0,
`eslint` 10.12.0, `@types/node` 24.12.4, `vite` 8.3.2, `vitest` 5.0.3, `fast-check` 4.10.2, `esbuild` 0.28.2, `tsx`
4.23.15, `playwright-core` 1.60.0 (C-0051), `clipper2-wasm` 0.4.0 (BSL-1.0, oracle), `polygon-clipping` 0.15.7 (MIT,
oracle). No prerelease in the production closure; the licence checker runs over it in the PR tier, and reports every
dev exception with its reason (`tools/notices/dev-exceptions.json`).

**The lint of §6.5 (3) (M0-d-07, wave 1).** In `kernel`, `model`, `tables`, `site`, `layout` (and every file whose output
reaches a digest): `Math` members only `abs floor ceil round trunc sign min max sqrt imul clz32 fround`; `**` forbidden
(C-0008); no `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance`, timers, `crypto.getRandomValues`, DOM, `toLocaleString`,
`localeCompare`, `Intl`; `Array.prototype.sort` only with a comparator; no `for…in`, `Object.keys/values/entries`
(C-0009; `Map` / `Set` insertion order allowed); the division rule (C-0044); the dependency direction; the repository
path rule with symbolic links resolved (§17.1 (3)); no bare `pnpm` in scripts, spawn literals and the command lines of
the Markdown files outside the records (C-0030; C-0093's scope). The vendored scan is the same
`Math` census over `vendor/*/` with its report and the audit record. **The probe** (C-0063, its mechanism C-0106): the
fixture `tools/lint/fixtures/probe/zz-probe.ts` — the checker's own probe of 2026-10-03, which the empty plugin passed —
is linted IN PLACE by the plugin's whole-tree check `probe-red` under the model-package rule set on every
`corepack pnpm lint`, which passes only when every planted line is reported; the check is the lint's acceptance test,
quoted by every model-package item's checker, and no file is ever copied into a package folder (four seats share one
tree).

**Commands** (the only forms documented): `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
(or `corepack pnpm install:frozen`) · `corepack pnpm build` · `corepack pnpm test` · `corepack pnpm lint` ·

## 5 Open questions the design leaves to M0 — decided (J122, J154)

1. **What is "a B-CITY city" before M1?** The spike city and schema-shaped synthetic records (C-0015); re-run at M1.
2. **Which of S3 do the spikes build?** The slice of C-0032 (lattice, picks, routes, `T`, level sets, gates, trace, the
   plaza); the rest M1.
3. **How does S8 meet a wall before S7 exists?** The strip stand-in of C-0033 — S7's own setback and glacis lines, laid
   by the trace strategy one milestone early, so no lane is planned through the band.
4. **What band does the fusion spike's S8 read without S6?** The synthetic ramp of C-0034, and the integrated run with
   S6's real pass-1 field reported beside it.
5. **How does S6 type without a roster?** The synthetic demand of C-0035.
6. **What does the substitution rung do without an allocation?** A `court` block, counted as residue (C-0036).
7. **Is §3.9 M0's or M1's?** The arena block is M0's (B-FUZZ's property and the renumbering test read it); the document
   is M1's (C-0037).
8. **Is "the whole constructive set" literally whole at M0?** No — by the design's own dates (§3.3's carve fixtures at
   M3a); M0 runs every class whose mechanism it builds and tags the rest with their milestones (C-0038).
9. **Which `dmath` routines?** Exactly those M0's code reads (C-0039); more as readers land.
10. **Which libraries are vendored at M0?** Five: `robust-predicates`, `flatbush`, `flatqueue` (flatbush's own
    dependency — no PLAT code imports it; our heap stands), `delaunator`, `simplex-noise` (C-0040, C-0052, C-0055).
11. **Transient arenas now or later?** M6-P, with the types declared now (C-0041).
12. **What is M0's exit record?** `M0-record.md` + `M0-record.json` in §13.3's shape (C-0042).
13. **How do NG's recorded shapes reach the PR tier?** As `ng-faces.json`, a numbers-only crossing file M-1 delivers
    (C-0043); routed to the fix list; the fallback if M-1 cannot deliver it is C-0071's.
14. **Which lints at M0?** The division rule yes, the unit lint at M1 with the schemas (C-0044).
15. **How much of `ChainProfile` at M0?** Reading, cutting and joining; the Write protocol at M2b (C-0045).
16. **How is a timing's standing decided?** By measurement, never by declaration (C-0047).
17. **How much of S1 at M0?** Terrain, hydrology, the river, basic crossing sites, water faces, outfalls, basic resources
    (C-0048).
18. **Where do `FieldBands`' shares come from before S2?** The band set's default household shares (C-0049).
19. **Which Node runs the x86 leg?** The universal binary's x86_64 slice under Rosetta 2 (C-0028); no download.
20. **Which Playwright?** `playwright-core` 1.60.0, the one release whose three browsers are all in the cache (C-0051);
    each launched once by the scaffold (CONFIRMED). Should a cached browser refuse to launch later, that leg is reported
    blocked by the owner's no-download rule and the download is asked of the owner — never faked.
21. **Where does `plat/` live?** In the Maps repository until the owner names its host (C-0031).
22. **How are the 16-core tier budgets judged on 8 cores?** Projected from CPU time (C-0027) until a runner exists.
23. **How does the `Seam` record look before II.1?** Minimal, with portals (C-0046).
24. **Where does the §3.7 "S11 geometry share" bar run without S11?** On a synthetic per-plot workload of the kernel
    calls §3.7 names; re-measured at M1 (§1 (a)).
25. **Which stage registers which `txForm` at M0?** As §4.1 states: callback for S5c and S8; declared for S3's slice, S4,
    S5a, S5b; S1 and S6 callback ("always safe"). The table that registers them is M0-x-04's.
26. **When does the lint land relative to the code it governs?** First: wave 1, alone (C-0063); the checker's probe is
    its acceptance and every model-package checker repeats it.
27. **Where does `@plat/model` re-export `H128` / `H32`?** In `model/src/digest/index.ts`, M0-d-04's; earlier readers
    import `@plat/kernel` (C-0066).
28. **Where does noise live?** In `@plat/kernel` (`src/noise` + the adapter), as §14 says (C-0065).
29. **What happens to a module folder the scaffold did not plan?** Its owner appends the one index line (C-0064); the
    three this spec plans are the scaffold fix round's.
30. **Which dependencies does the build add to §17.4's table?** eslint, typescript-eslint, @types/node, vite (dev) and
    flatqueue (production, through flatbush) — recorded and routed to the fix list (C-0062); testkit's oracles are dev.
31. **What does the parity CLI do without `baselines.json`?** It stops naming the file (§13.5's T-RIG-1); the parity
    job and the record's entry are pending-after-M-1 (C-0068).
32. **How does a tier carry a job whose input M-1 has not delivered?** As an `after-M-1: <file>` entry, pending, never
    pass; a built job with a missing input fails by §13.8's edge (C-0069). The deny-list scan is M0-k-06.
33. **Who checks M0's calibratable cells with the register?** M1, when the register lands; M0 marks and enumerates them
    (C-0070).
34. **What runs if M-1 commits `baselines.json` and the digest without `ng-faces.json`?** The (a) items; the (b) items
    wait, and become descriptive by the ⟨M-1⟩ rule if M-1 records it cannot deliver the file (C-0071).
35. **Which MFCG street-signature rows gate at M0?** T / Y share, intramural dead ends, blocks per ha; R4 and wall
    alignment are proxies, lots per block M1's (C-0072).
36. **Are the corner and arrival clauses judged now?** Yes, on the M0 (b) faces (C-0073), and re-run on NG's shapes by
    M0-b-05b (C-0081); σ and the fillet share wait.
37. **Where is §12.1's in-Chrome re-measure?** For the fusion and site gates, in M0's timing phase: Node and Chromium's
    worker on the same seeds, the Chromium figure checked past ± 15 % (C-0082, superseding C-0074); for §12.3's model
    budgets, M1's nightly.
38. **When is the reference score recorded?** As the timing-phase wave's first act (C-0075); null before it.
39. **How does S4 cross the river in the site spike?** Through a crossing site's deck; the `Bridge` becomes `built`
    (C-0076).
40. **How are the pipeline and the tiers split across waves?** Registry and runner early over fixture stages, the base
    table last (C-0077); the tier runner and PR tier early, the nightly and milestone contents after the harnesses
    (C-0079); the façade does not wait for the arena block or the medial axis (C-0078).
41. **Where may a bench read its inputs?** Inside `plat/` or in-process only; outputs and full reports go to
    `PLAT_BENCH_OUT`, numbers-only summaries to `docs/build/summaries/` (C-0067).
42. **What follows a timing miss?** The owning item applies the bar's pre-decided fallback in a fix round (T-fix), and
    M0-t-02 re-measures exactly the missed bars alone (T2) before the M0 record (C-0080).
43. **Where does T34-1 run?** Its commit clause (blocks below τ, cut faces at or above it, replayed from the `cut.stop`
    draws) at M0-b-03 in the PR tier; its 10 000-face mean nightly at M0-b-04; the τ formula's range is M0-b-02's unit
    test, not T34-1 (the checker's SP-r1-01).
44. **Is R12-4 an M0 bar?** Yes — reported in the timing phase from the two spikes' per-stage stamps; an exceeding row
    is restated by M0-x-01 in a choices row; no fallback, no T-fix (C-0084).
45. **Where is §13.1's ladder coverage checked, and what are F-WORK's rungs?** The kernel ladders at M0-k-04; every
    stage rung M0 builds at M0-x-05 after the stages land; each stage's declared coarser rung on `E_WORK_LIMIT` is
    C-0085's list (hydrology coarsens, the fields coarsen, the proposal queue closes, the leftover rule, the recursion
    stops, the route goes unserved).
46. **What reference do the block-area and cut-length KS use?** `ng-faces.json`'s per-face block areas and cut lengths
    and a cut-lengths-per-face baseline row, both requested of M-1; absent, the clause is descriptive by the ⟨M-1⟩ rule
    (C-0086).
47. **How does the site spike's trace meet the river?** At a basic water gate — the trace's two shore vertices carry
    `gate_end`, the `Gate` has `banks` and no way, not counted in N; the rest of §4.4's paragraph is M1's (C-0087).
48. **How are the tiers timed without the nightly timing the nightly?** The nightly's last job is §13.8's nightly
    timing-phase contents, `not-built: M1`; `bench:timing-phase` is the M0 exit's own run (C-0088); the tiers are timed by
    C-0097's protocol — `tier:pr` gating on its batched sum plus one whole run, the projected tiers once whole with one
    bounded repeat, the detector sampled throughout — and the T wave needs ≈ 4.5–7 h of idle machine, at most ≈ 8–12 h
    with every repeat (C-0097 supersedes C-0088's whole-tier timing; C-0119).
49. **Who builds `resolveVertexAt`?** M2a, its first reader; at M0 a `notBuilt('M2a')` stub with `CarryMap` declared
    (C-0089).
50. **What workload does the matching bar time?** M0-d-09's 20 re-derivation pairs of the spike city (a scoped reroll
    of S5 through the runner's `rerolls` option), old and fresh per kind, beside M0-d-05b's synthetic sets (C-0090).
51. **What does M0-f-03b read?** The four harness summaries' per-counter work-per-unit quantiles, inside `plat/`; never
    `PLAT_BENCH_OUT` (C-0091).
52. **What is M0-k-05's form of the parts V12 defines?** The band rule from the row's stored p10 / p90 and `spreadKS`,
    sign-indefinite or floored rows `notApplicable` never pass; checks C1–C7 from §17.1 (4)'s text, C8–C10 named as not
    run; a minimal `CrossingRecord` in `crossings.json`; V12's definitions enter at M1 (C-0092).
53. **What does `no-bare-pnpm` scan?** Package scripts, spawn literals, and fenced or inline command lines in the
    Markdown files outside the records; never `docs/build/**`, `CLEAN-ROOM.md`, `packageManager` or prose (C-0093).
54. **Are the junction median and the organic 4-way share judged now?** Yes, by M0-c-06 beside p5 ≥ 30°; M0-c-07a
    re-judges them against M-1's recomputed band (C-0094).
55. **How are the scaffold's two latent test defects and the missing hand-overs fixed?** A second scaffold fix round
    (`build/m0-scaffold-fix2`, landed, L-0011) and the four hand-overs of C-0095.
56. **Where does B-EDGE run at M0, and §13.1's per-class degenerate inputs?** In M0-x-06 (wave 17): §4.13's EP-01 on
    every M0 stage × five kinds, EP-04, EP-05, EP-06, EP-16's stop-test end, EP-20's and EP-23's M0 parts, the frame cells
    for river, bridge and wall, and five kinds × eight classes, each fixture the smallest state reaching its home, at
    `PLAT_EDGE_SEEDS` (10 PR, 1 000 nightly), the home's outcome hard, 0 per 1 000; the rest listed with its milestone
    (C-0100).
57. **Can M0-k-02 judge the constructive set in wave 7?** No — it enumerates, states each case's expected outcome and
    runs the numeric-core cases; M0-k-04 (wave 11, after the arena block too) runs every M0 case green (C-0110).
58. **Why wait for M-1 to build the scanner?** We do not: M0-k-06 builds and tests it now on a synthetic deny-list (wave
    13); M0-k-07 runs it over M-1's file; the normalisation is fixed on our side (`normalisationVersion` 1) and requested
    of M-1 as the file's format; the `ng-faces.json` loader is M0-k-05's now (C-0101).
59. **May an AFTER-M-1 item start during the timing phase or as a fifth seat?** Never: every AFTER-M-1 item depends on
    M0-x-01 (after T, T-fix and T2) and takes only a seat the open wave leaves free (C-0102).
60. **Does the contention detector see M-1's lane?** Yes: it counts every browser, node, python, bench, tsc, vitest and
    esbuild process on the machine and any process at ≥ 10 % CPU outside the harness's own tree, and the session opens
    the phase only after M-1's seats are paused, with a token the script requires and records (C-0103).
61. **How is a tier timed on a fanless machine?** `tier:pr` (the one gating tier) on its batched sum — ≤ 60 s batches
    with calibrate before and after, a drifting batch re-run at most twice then `throttled` — plus one whole run
    reported; the projected tiers once whole, one repeat, then `throttled`; never a loop (C-0097).
62. **Which of §3.7's two miss paths applies to the band and S11 bars, and in what order?** One ordered ladder for every
    kernel bar: optimise → amend (≤ 2×) or accelerate (> 2×) → for the arrangement bars Clipper2-WASM as the only engine,
    for the others the D-18 re-declaration; at most three cycles (C-0098).
63. **Two `ladderCoverage()` exports?** No: M0-x-05 exports `stageLadderCoverage()` and merges M0-k-04's report (C-0109).
64. **How does a checker attribute a diff when four seats share one tree and run no git?** By landed records against the
    wave's snapshot — `corepack pnpm snapshot`, `landed`, `landed:verify` from the scaffold's third fix round — with the
    appends exempted under the id rule (C-0104); the probe runs in place as the lint's `probe-red` check (C-0106).
65. **Who builds the synthetic S11 workload?** M0-k-04, with a call-count test; M0-t-01 only measures it (C-0107).
66. **Who owns T34-1's 10 000-face mean?** M0-b-04 alone (C-0108).
67. **Are the tiers' end-to-end runs vitest tests?** No — command receipts of the checker; the vitest tests run the runner
    over fixture manifests (C-0105), and a job's status is derived at run time, never written on landing (C-0099).
68. **Where do the types the kernel reads live, when §14 declares some of them in a layout block?** In `@plat/kernel`:
    `kernel/src/types/` (M0-a-01) and `Hash64` / `Hash128` in `kernel/src/hash/` (M0-d-02), re-exported by `@plat/model`
    under their design names; M0-m-01 moves to wave 3 and no kernel item depends on it (C-0112).
69. **What runs `plat parity`, `plat baselines check` and the scan before a `plat` bin exists?** The dispatcher entries
    `parity`, `baselines-check` and `scan` with the root shortcuts `corepack pnpm parity`, `baselines:check -- <file>` and
    `scan`, owned by M0-k-05 and M0-k-06 as thin entries over testkit's code; the bin is M1's `@plat/api` (C-0113).
70. **Where does a test of bench code live?** In `bench/test/<harness>/`, owned by the harness folder's owner — the only
    test project that references the bench (C-0114).
71. **Who builds the timing-phase script, and when?** M0-t-00, in wave 17, tested on fixture bars with planted timings and
    checked before wave T opens; M0-t-01 is a run item that runs it alone (C-0115).
72. **What does the parity CLI report for an ⟨M-1⟩ cell with no row?** `fail`, never `missingBaseline` or `pass`; a cell
    M-1 could not measure crosses as a descriptive row and is `reported`; `missingBaseline` is for a non-⟨M-1⟩ metric with
    no row. The ⟨M-1⟩ cells are marked in `METRICS` (C-0116).
73. **Is the NG and MFCG comparison code AFTER-M-1?** No — M0-b-05 (wave 14) and M0-c-07 (wave 17) build and test the
    harnesses now on synthetic files; M0-b-05a, M0-b-05b, M0-c-07a and M0-c-07b run them over M-1's files (C-0117).
74. **Does the cliff × frame cell run at M0?** Yes — its M0 part (the rasters and the L0 batch clipped at the arena's
    outer ring) in M0-x-06; the drawn clause is M1's (C-0118).
75. **How are the four stale texts corrected?** By C-0119 (C-0102's wave, M0-a-01's checker, item 48 above, `CLEAN-ROOM.md`
    rule 6), with rule 6 edited in place by the spec lane that wrote it.

76. **When may M-1's files cross into `plat/` while M0's waves run, and who is answerable for them?** In an open build
    or AFTER-M-1 wave, never in T, T-fix or T2 and never between a wave's close and the next snapshot, a numbers-only file
    after M0-k-05 has LANDED; each with its `CrossingRecord` appended by the countersigning seat and its ledger row, the
    file attributed by that record at the wave's close, the record and the `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2 – §5 rows claimed by their
    seats' landed records (C-0120).
77. **Does a tier job flip to built the moment M-1's file exists?** No: a job declaring `reviewedBy` stays `after-M-1:
    <file> (review pending: <item>)` until each reviewer's summary names the file's sha256 — the deny-list scan until
    M0-k-07, the parity report until M0-b-05a and M0-c-07a (C-0121).
78. **What do T's tier timings include when an M-1 file already exists?** Exactly the jobs built when the phase opens
    (no crossing lands during T): the deny-list scan inside `tier:pr`'s gating figure only when the list crossed and
    M0-k-07 reviewed it before T, else listed pending and never timed, the PR tier with the scan timed at M1; the parity
    report never at M0; M0-k-07 therefore starts in the first open build wave after the crossing (C-0121).
79. **Where does a test of package code that reads `@plat/testkit` code live?** In the testkit test project —
    `packages/testkit/test/<package>/<item folder>/`, owned by the package item and named in its tests — the one package
    test project that references every package (the closing check CONFIRMED that `kernel/test` and `layout/test` cannot
    compile such an import); the item exports what the test reads through `@plat/<package>`, so `arr/index.ts` passes
    M0-a-08 → M0-a-09; the aggregate B-FUZZ runs stay M0-k-04's; a package test project never references the test kit
    (C-0122).
80. **How does M0-e-03's stage test run when `@plat/site` cannot import the layout's runner?** Under a hand-built
    `StageContext` (the model's type) over the kernel's façade; M0-x-02 leaves its `dependsOn`; the runner-based S1 runs
    are M0-x-04's and M0-e-06's. The other dependency records corrected with it: M0-k-05 → M0-a-10, the kernel and layout
    items' testkit inputs (M0-k-01, M0-k-02, M0-k-05), M0-x-03's own `startsWhen`; no wave moved (C-0123).

Nothing is left open.

## 6 The open design findings (`open-design-findings.md`) — every row decided

The twelve findings touch mechanisms M0 does not build; none changes an M0 item. Each is **not affecting M0**, with the
reason and the milestone whose build follows the fix (the design text is corrected later from the fix list):

| finding | decision | why |
|---|---|---|
| VF7y-GEN-03 (F-WALL's raised-way rung, §4.13's wall cell and §5.4's `W_RAISED_MEETING` list two of law 2 (c)'s outcomes unevenly) | not affecting M0 | raised ways and law 2 (c) are M3a's; M0's F-WALL ladder (M0-c-02) implements the trace and gate rungs only and emits no `W_RAISED_MEETING`; the M3a build lists both outcomes (the cross wall and the top-up's arc) as the fix states |
| VF7y-GEN-04 (T110-2 (6)'s fixture cannot hold its state; W3·C2) | not affecting M0 | T110-2 is M3a's (§13.8); M0 has no aqueduct, no regeneration and no placement lock |
| VF7y-HND-01 (§7.1's aqueduct-course row cites a narrower law set) | not affecting M0 | hand edits are M2a / M3a's; the M3a build takes the full set (law 1 (2)–(6), (9)–(11), law 2 (a), law 3) |
| VF7y-HND-02 (a warp's or revert's moved stretch has no bend row on the wall's side) | not affecting M0 | M0 builds the kernel's `warp` (M0-a-13), whose semantics the finding does not touch; the edit layer's bend lines are M3a's |
| VF7y-HND-03 (T110-2 (4) has no hand `refuse.raised.meeting` variant) | not affecting M0 | M3a's test |
| VF7y-TST-02 (four law-2 outcomes run by no bar) | not affecting M0 | M3a, V-M3 and E3 clauses |
| VF7y-TST-03 (F-SITE's cross-wall rung and test cell; F-BUDGET-STAGE's test cell) | not affecting M0 | F-SITE's nuclei rungs are S3 (1)'s polycentric forms, M1's (C-0032); M0's S5d top-up (M0-c-05) has no raised way, so the kept-arc clause does not arise; the M1 build takes the corrected cells |
| VAH-r6-03 (§7.7 item 1's "one `DossierChange` per changed element" lacks §4.11 (4)'s exception) | not affecting M0 | the port's absorb half is M3a's |
| VAP-r6-03 (which derived dossier fixtures take a manifest row) | not affecting M0 | the frozen dossier fixtures and their manifest are M1's |
| VCS-r6-05 (`DossierFixtureRow`'s `file` and `derivedFrom` comments) | not affecting M0 | M1's test-kit type |
| G127-determinism-01 (owner rule 127's switch list not applied to §7.1's dry run, §7.4, §7.6, §7.8) | not affecting M0 | item 127 adds edit kinds and switches, no stage, concern or kernel op; M0's registries (M0-d-01) need no reservation for it; applied when the build reaches §7 (M2a / M3a) |
| G127-scope-01 (§13.2 lacks item 127 (e)'s bars) | not affecting M0 | the bars accompany those edits |
